citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked vector the sample/approximate-entropy, SVD-entropy, Katz and moments cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioEEG::multiscaleEntropy (scales 1-8, m=2, r=0.2*SD fixed on the original signal): the sample entropy of the coarse-grained (non-overlapping-window means) signal at each scale. The reference re-computes the per-scale curve with NeuroKit2 entropy_multiscale (MSEn), via reticulate; a white-noise series (same N, matched SD) is computed for the structure contrast. Deterministic.
note: multiscaleEntropy is a NEW standalone op that completes the entropy family in PhysioEEG (sample/approximate/permutation/SVD/dispersion/increment/slope entropies + Lempel-Ziv); MSE previously existed only inside eegComplexity. It reproduces NeuroKit2 entropy_multiscale (MSEn) BIT-FOR-BIT across scales 1-8 (max |diff| ~4e-16) -- the identical coarse-graining and fixed-tolerance sample entropy. Finding: the MSE curve is NON-MONOTONIC, rising from scale 1 (1.327) to a peak at scale 5 (1.879, ~31 ms at 160 Hz) and exceeding the scale-1 value; a white-noise series of the same length and SD instead FALLS monotonically (2.16 at scale 1 to 1.08 at scale 8), so the rise is the signature of genuine multi-scale structure in the eyes-closed EEG (fast activity plus slower alpha-band dynamics), cross-consistent with the SVD-entropy (low-dimensional structure) and sample-entropy cases. Caveat: at coarse scales the coarse-grained series is short (scale 8 leaves 200 points), so high-scale SampEn is less stable; MSE beyond scale ~10 would need a longer segment.
